analysis.investment_thesis: IXIGO is riding India's structural travel digitization wave with a dominant train-ticketing position and impressive 39% YoY revenue growth to ₹914 Cr, but at 133x trailing P/E with only 7% operating margins and a net profit decline in FY25, the market is pricing in flawless execution the company hasn't yet consistently demonstrated. I'd admire the business model but wait for margin maturity before committing capital.
key_strengths: Dominant train-ticketing moat via ixigo + ConfirmTkt + AbhiBus trio, addressing India's most-searched travel segment
Platform economics shine through 81.74% gross margin — the asset-light OTA model scales beautifully
Balance sheet is rock solid (D/E 0.04) and FCF turned strongly positive at ₹118 Cr in FY25 after years of cash burn
key_risks: Operating margins are a thin 7% — any competitive price war with MakeMyTrip or IRCTC direct could eliminate profitability entirely
Net profit fell 18% YoY (₹73 Cr → ₹60 Cr in FY25) while revenue grew 39% — costs scaling faster than revenue is a Fisher warning sign
At 133x trailing P/E and 119x EV/EBITDA, the valuation tolerates zero disappointment; even a modest growth deceleration could be punishing
red_flags: FY24 profits were flattered by ₹39 Cr 'other income' (likely IPO-related treasury gains) that collapsed to ₹23 Cr in FY25 — underlying profitability is weaker than headline suggests
ROE of only 9.74% is far below my 20% threshold; the post-IPO equity infusion has diluted returns and management hasn't yet deployed capital productively
OCF positive in only 3 of last 5 years — operational cash generation is still maturing
analysis.detailed_analysis:
IXIGO is a genuinely interesting growth story anchored to one of the world's largest and most underpenetrated travel markets. India's 10 billion annual rail journeys alone represent a massive TAM, and ixigo's multi-modal platform — trains, flights, buses, hotels — positions it to capture a broader share of the Indian traveller's wallet over time. The 6-year revenue CAGR of 68.5% is extraordinary, though COVID-recovery tailwinds inflate that figure; the more telling stat is a still-robust 39% growth in FY25 as a ₹914 Cr business. The gross margin of 81.74% confirms the platform's pricing power and asset-light character — exactly the kind of scalable economics I look for when scuttlebutting a business.

However, my discipline demands that great businesses be purchased at sensible prices, and here I find myself restrained. The FY25 profit decline from ₹73 Cr to ₹60 Cr, while revenue surged, signals that investment in growth (customer acquisition, product, AI features) is outpacing monetisation — acceptable in early innings, but IXIGO is 20 years old and recently public. Management quality appears competent but unproven at scale; the reliance on other income to prop up FY24 profits is a qualitative concern. At 57x forward P/E (even the optimistic analyst consensus), the stock requires sustained 30%+ earnings growth for years — achievable, but not certain enough for me to buy aggressively today. I'd watch operating margins cross 12-15% sustainably before adding meaningfully.
